name: Manav Infra Projects Limited
summary:
**Hold — unresolved.** Manav is a recovering, small foundation and construction-services contractor, not yet a demonstrated compounder. FY26 contract revenue grew 69.6% to ₹41.56 crore. Actual piling and anchoring orders, repeat customer access and investment in machinery support the operating recovery. They do not establish a defensible moat, a funded growth plan or an executable investment.

The decisive concerns are more specific than a generic SME discount: repeated depreciation-note inconsistencies, low recent cash realization, a cash balance of only ₹0.134 crore at the last audited date, seasonal funding needs and extremely thin observed trading. No fraud, bank default or diversion is established by the records reviewed. Low leverage and clean statutory audit annexures are meaningful counterevidence.

The historical scoring assessment is BQS 5.3 and GQS 6.4, both excluded from numerical quality rankings while financial reliability is unresolved. IAS is NS. At the stale authenticated ₹38.75 reference, the explicitly equity-funded base alternative returns about 7.7% annually over 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, below the 15% hurdle. It is not an ordinary investor return or an investable entry range: the ordinary and non-rescue paths are unsupported. A lower share price alone cannot solve the missing funding and execution evidence.

IAS.gate_exclusion: G2/G3/G4 unresolved; R and L are NS. Bounds are arithmetic, not ratings.

GOV.rationale: Clean formal oversight, but mixed reporting discipline and thin related-party detail.
material_facts: Main, IFC and CARO conclusions are clean; auditor change was normal rotation.
The rights issue and director financing are disclosed; remuneration ceilings require monitoring.
GOV.counterevidence: Repeated financial-note errors prevent a high stewardship score.

MOAT.rationale: Repeat relationships and specialist equipment matter, but durable exclusionary economics are unproven.
material_facts: Kanakia appears in the 2017 customer list and a 2026 amended contract.
Ground engineering requires site competence, but outsourced contract expense is 60.1% of sales.
MOAT.counterevidence: Repeat customers and a 16.2% core EBITDA margin are positives, not proof of pricing power.

REV.rationale: FY23–FY26 comparable revenue CAGR is 51.5%; the starting score 9 is limited to 8 by medium confidence and recovery distortion.
material_facts: FY21–FY26 CAGR is 52.4%, but starts in the pandemic trough.
Both FY26 halves grew, by 48.4% and 77.1%, without an identified acquisition.
REV.counterevidence: The long-cycle FY16 endpoint proxy is only 9.7%; billing and outsourcing affect reported revenue. No trajectory adjustment is added.

DUR.rationale: Repeat foundation work offers accessible growth, but disclosed visibility is short.
material_facts: March backlog is approximately ₹18 crore, 0.43× FY26 sales.
Verified Adani, Kanakia, Kolte Patil and JSW letters evidence access to actual work.
DUR.counterevidence: No backlog rollforward, project margin or complete execution calendar is disclosed.

CAP.rationale: Multi-year incremental returns are meaningful, but recent deployment has not yet earned its cost.
material_facts: FY23–FY26 incremental NOPAT/IC is 22.1%; FY24–FY26 is 18.2%, against a 14–18% analytical capital-cost range.
FY26 incremental return is 6.3% after ₹8.90 crore additional capital and ₹4.995 crore capex.
CAP.counterevidence: Young capex may mature; lack of private project cohorts alone is not grounds for NS.

CASH.rationale: Cash conversion is mixed after classification corrections, not persistent collapse or clean compounding.
material_facts: Three-year conversion is 72.0% after interest and debt recast, or 70.3% after sale-sign reconstruction; four-year conversion is 86.3%.
FY26 after-interest CFO is ₹0.454 crore versus PAT ₹4.026 crore, with receivables ₹10.905 crore.
CASH.counterevidence: Aged receivables declined in absolute terms, and reported CFO is depressed by included debt repayment.

BAL.rationale: Low accounting leverage coexists with very thin cash and scheduled maturities.
material_facts: Net-debt/core-EBITDA is 0.83× and core EBIT/interest is 5.88×.
Bank cash is ₹0.0216 crore against annual principal ₹1.1484 crore; the seasonal forecast requires finance.
BAL.counterevidence: Debt declined ₹1.593 crore and CARO reports neither default nor a material one-year-liability uncertainty.

EXEC.rationale: Revenue and machinery deployment demonstrate recovery, not yet consistent full-cycle delivery.
material_facts: Revenue grew from ₹11.95 crore to ₹41.56 crore in FY23–FY26 with repeat named orders.
FY25/FY26 capex was ₹2.8124/₹4.9950 crore, a tangible deployment commitment.
EXEC.counterevidence: Project utilization, planned-versus-actual completion and new-capex return cohorts are ND; pandemic losses were severe.

EARN.rationale: Underlying profit grew, but interest, taxes, margins and dilution complicate EPS.
material_facts: Core EBITDA rose ₹5.362 crore to ₹6.719 crore while margin fell 21.9% to 16.2%.
PBT growth of ₹1.516 crore includes ₹0.629 crore lower finance cost; same-share PAT grew 25.1%.
EARN.counterevidence: Reported EPS ₹3.06 versus ₹4.66 reflects the rights-weighted denominator; normalized PAT is only ₹3.249 crore.

R.rationale: Ordinary base return is not scoreable while reliability, funding and execution remain unresolved.
material_facts: All three central non-rescue forecasts breach the reserve before entry.
The explicit funded base returns 7.7%, below 15%, but no financing commitment is evidenced.
R.counterevidence: Actual collections or a committed facility could restore scoreability; unknown is not replaced with an arbitrary low score.

D.rationale: Linked stress creates impairment and recapitalization risk, not evidenced insolvency.
material_facts: The funded bear ends around ₹14.79 per share with a negative annual return.
Collection, equipment spending and maturities interact while exit liquidity is poor.
D.counterevidence: Low leverage, clean CARO and repeat business are real support, but not cash equivalents.

P.rationale: The reference price requires sustained growth beyond the base case.
material_facts: ₹38.75 implies 15.7× normalized earnings and 8.42× core EBITDA enterprise value.
A funded 15% hurdle reverse case requires 20.85% annual growth at 16% margin and 6× exit EBITDA.
P.counterevidence: This is below recent recovery growth but above the 9.7% long-cycle endpoint proxy; a bull outcome is possible, not proven.

L.rationale: Incomplete full-window statistics and whole-lot constraints prevent a valid liquidity score.
material_facts: Only 27 of 60 authenticated archives have an issuer row.
No observed date supports one whole lot at 5% participation; the latest row is 5 October.
L.counterevidence: Trading at higher participation is a different assumption and cannot establish a dependable exit.

gates.reason: No substantiated diversion, fraud or default was identified. Disclosed rights and director loans are not intrinsically abusive; reporting and RPT detail remain mixed.
gates.release_condition: Consistent capital/ownership disclosures and quantified related-party loan terms.

gates.reason: Repeated material PPE-note discrepancies, asset-sale cash-flow classification and unspecified investment detail require reconciliation. The main and IFC opinions are clean and net PPE ties; this is not a fraud finding.
gates.release_condition: Issuer/auditor reconciliation of PPE charges, disposal rollforwards, cash-flow signs and the ₹0.974 crore investment, plus reliable interim accounts.

gates.reason: March cash of ₹0.134 crore and seasonal working-capital, capex and maturity assumptions produce a pre-entry funding shortfall. Current committed finance and the actual bridge are unverified. Clean CARO xix found no material uncertainty about one-year liabilities, meaningful counterevidence; this is not an observed default.
gates.release_condition: A verified current cash, collections, capex and gross-obligations bridge, with committed funding where required under stress.

gates.release_condition: A current exact-security quote, applicable lot/restriction checks and full recent turnover supporting realistic whole-lot execution.

sections.title: Research header, gates and data confidence
sections.text:
Legal issuer: **Manav Infra Projects Limited**. NSE Emerge symbol **MANAV**, ISIN **INE104Y01012**, CIN **L45200MH2009PLC193084**. Incorporation: 8 June 2009. Do not confuse it with Man Infraconstruction/MANINFRA or similarly named private businesses. The promoter's earlier operating history is not the listed company's incorporation date.

Cutoff: **20 October 2026**. Financial scope: standalone audited March-year-end accounts, with six annual observations FY21–FY26. No subsidiary, associate or consolidation perimeter requiring a group calculation was identified. The issuer describes Ind AS adoption; some policy and segment wording is inconsistent boilerplate. We do not silently relabel the basis as ordinary AS because it trades on SME.

Price: **₹38.75 on 5 October 2026**, not a 19 October closing quote. The exact dated official row is the last observed in the 60-session window ending 19 October. Issued shares: **13,160,000**, ₹10 face value. Implied capitalization: **₹50.995 crore**, using that stale reference. Lot: **4,000 shares**, independently present in the observed exchange rows and corroborated by the official security-master URL dated 19 October, retrieved on 22 October; its cutoff surveillance state is not independently established. Five-year equity hurdle: nominal 15%, before personal taxes. Illustrative liquidity position: ₹500,000, not a suggested allocation.

| Gate | Status | Decision-relevant condition |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Conditional | No substantiated abuse; require better RPT and capital disclosure. |
| G2 | Hold — unresolved | Reconcile PPE/CFS discrepancies and the unidentified investment. |
| G3 | Hold — unresolved | Demonstrate the March-to-entry cash and obligations bridge. |
| G4 | Hold — unresolved | Verify current tradability and feasible whole-lot execution. |

Confidence is high in identity, dated exchange rows and transcription of the main annual P&L. It is medium in organic growth and normalized multi-year capital returns, low in current funding and forward margins, and insufficient for a full 60-session liquidity score. No statement here treats an assumed cash reserve as a statutory requirement or a modeled deficit as an actual missed payment.

BQS = 0.20×5 + 0.20×4 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×5 + 0.10×5 + 0.08×4 + 0.08×6 = **5.26**, displayed 5.3. GQS = 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×5 + 0.15×5 + 0.10×5 = **6.40**, displayed 6.4. No governance, funding-failure or persistent-value-destruction numerical cap is invoked without the corresponding evidence. Historical ratings remain conditional analytical assessments, not permission to rank an unreliable company as investable.

IAS uses unrounded BQS 5.26, not its displayed 5.3. Known contribution is 2.3150; R and L are NS, leaving 45% missing. Unimputed bounds are **2.7650 to 6.8150**. These are mathematical bounds, not a substitute score. Unknown factors are neither assigned five nor removed and reweighted. G2 and G4 independently prevent a favorable new-purchase classification.

REV's selected post-lockdown FY23–FY26 window is stated before scoring. The ≥30% schedule starts at 9, no trajectory point is added, and the medium-confidence/history ceiling limits the factor to 8. The 52.4% five-year reported growth and 9.7% long-cycle endpoint proxy are both shown rather than hiding inconvenient periods. CAP and CASH are not scored NS merely because private project cohorts or daily bank statements are unavailable: their public multi-year bridges support mixed scores.

sections.title: Business overview
sections.text:
Manav earns contract income from civil and infrastructure services, especially excavation, piling, rock anchoring, micro-piling, basement and associated groundwork. It also has a history of machinery rental and earth-moving services, but FY26 accounts disclose all operating revenue as contract income, not a separately measured rental segment. The verified 2026 projects are predominantly Mumbai redevelopment and specialist foundation jobs. This is not evidence of a national integrated EPC franchise or of owning the underlying real estate.

Customers buy completion of a site-specific task. Commercial economics depend on mobilization, equipment deployment, subcontractor and labour availability, fuel, certification of work, retention release and collections. The revenue policy recognizes site services as rendered over the contract and says measurement relies on management confirmation where completion is difficult to identify. Independent customer certification, billing milestones and subsequent cash receipts therefore matter more than a press release's headline order value.

The operating model is a hybrid of owned machinery and outsourced execution. FY26 contract expenses were ₹24.973 crore, about 60.1% of revenue, compared with approximately ₹9.47 crore or 38.7% in FY25. Fuel was ₹2.525 crore, labour ₹1.451 crore and machine hire ₹0.830 crore. Only 14 permanent employees were reported. Scaling is thus not simply 'number of machines × utilization': substantial output is procured externally, and supplier terms can shift cash requirements.

Gross PPE additions were ₹4.995 crore in FY26, of which plant and machinery ₹4.670 crore. Net PPE rose from ₹3.331 crore to ₹6.587 crore. This is actual investment, not just announced capacity. However, machine counts, rig utilization, job profitability, revenue per machine and replacement needs are not disclosed well enough to assert a capacity moat. Gross project profit is ND rather than invented by classifying only material purchases as cost of goods sold.

sections.title: Moat and industry position
sections.text:
A credible positive is repeat customer access: Kanakia appears in the 2017 prospectus and in a revised 2026 work order. Specialist ground engineering needs equipment, operating know-how, site safety and a record of execution. These can provide a useful local position. Yet no exclusive concession, proprietary technology, enduring price premium, contractual switching barrier or sustained superior incremental returns is demonstrated. A capable competitor can procure rigs, hire experienced operators and bid through similar channels. Capital and relationships are obstacles, not necessarily durable exclusion.

The 2017 prospectus said the top five customers supplied approximately 82% of revenue. That is dated historical evidence, not the current concentration ratio. FY26 customer percentages and customer-by-customer receivables are ND. The order announcements broaden the visible names but do not establish diversified revenue or cash collection. We reject unsourced contemporary website concentration numbers rather than carrying the 2017 figure forward.

Economic reference companies illustrate the spectrum, not a peer-multiple valuation shortcut:

| Reference | Period / scope | Revenue / EBITDA margin | Backlog | Relevance and limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| J. Kumar Infraprojects | FY25, reported operating group metrics | ₹5,693 crore / 14.5% | ₹22,238 crore | Large urban transport/tunnelling EPC; far greater qualification and capital capability. FY25 context, not latest FY26 valuation. |
| B.L. Kashyap & Sons | FY26 consolidated | ₹1,379.14 crore / 7.41% | About ₹5,000 crore in annual narrative | Building contractor with different project mix, legacy obligations and substantially larger scale. |
| Cemindia Projects, formerly ITD Cementation | FY26 consolidated | ₹10,061 crore / 11.9% | ₹24,545 crore | Foundation specialist inside a large multi-sector EPC platform; broad technical capability, not a close SME liquidity analogue. |

Manav's 16.2% normalized EBITDA margin is higher than these reported group margins, but it has much shorter disclosed backlog coverage, a different subcontracting mix, inconsistent note detail and a very small equity market. None of the peer market multiples is borrowed without a dated common-price comparison. The base 6× exit EV/EBITDA is an analyst assumption, tested at 4× and 8×, not a claimed market median.

sections.title: Revenue growth and scale
sections.text:
| FY ending March | Contract revenue ₹cr | Annual addition ₹cr | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 5.05 | ND | ND |
| 2022 | 5.39 | 0.34 | 6.8% |
| 2023 | 11.95 | 6.56 | 121.6% |
| 2024 | 14.31 | 2.36 | 19.8% |
| 2025 | 24.50 | 10.19 | 71.2% |
| 2026 | 41.56 | 17.06 | 69.6% |

FY21–FY26 reported CAGR is **52.4%**, from ₹5.05 crore to ₹41.56 crore. FY21 was severely affected by the pandemic, so this is not a normal starting utilization level. The selected FY23–FY26 post-lockdown comparison gives **51.5%**, from ₹11.95 crore, and contains four audited annual observations. It too contains recovery and should not be extended indefinitely. FY16 prospectus revenue of ₹16.4414 crore gives a **9.7% ten-year endpoint growth proxy**; intervening years are incomplete, so this is context, not a fully authenticated eleven-observation comparable annual series.

FY26 H1 revenue was ₹9.4288 crore versus an implied ₹6.3527 crore in FY25 H1, up 48.4%. FY26 H2 was ₹32.1289 crore versus ₹18.1446 crore, up 77.1%. H2 is the audited full-year less limited-reviewed H1 balancing figure, not an independently audited six-month set. Approximately 77.3% of FY26 revenue and 89.7% of PAT arrived in H2. Annualizing H1 or treating October-to-March work as evenly distributed would be misleading. No H1 FY27 financial result was verified as available by the cutoff; FY26 is the latest audited full-year anchor, not a reconstructed TTM with invented quarters.

There is no identified acquisition or merger driving this rise. Machinery investment, higher contract expenses and named work support organic contract execution. The company attributes growth to higher project execution and new jobs. But price versus volume, excavation versus piling mix, customer certifications and pass-through subcontract value are not separately measurable. Revenue expanded much faster than core EBITDA in FY26, so the topline alone overstates the improvement in economic output.

sections.title: Growth quality and reinvestment runway
sections.text:
The addressable opportunity is local redevelopment and infrastructure groundwork, not the entire national infrastructure budget. The relevant proof is accessible contracts and profitable conversion. March 2026 backlog was approximately ₹18 crore, just 0.43× FY26 sales. The annual report does not state whether it includes GST or provide an opening-plus-intake-minus-execution rollforward. It cannot be combined mechanically with all subsequent headline announcements to create a 'current order book'.

| Date | Customer / project counterparty | Announced gross ₹cr | Incremental ex-GST ₹cr, low–high | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-11 | Kolte Patil Developers | 2.99 | 1.02–2.54 | Extension wording ambiguous between revised total and additional order. Do not sum both without clarification. |
| 2026-05-17 | Adani Realty | 12.29 | 10.41–10.41 | New announced work; execution and cash terms ND |
| 2026-06-01 | Kanakia Spaces / Transparent Developers | 12.10 | 4.11–4.11 | Revised total; incremental difference only. |
| 2026-07-17 | JSW Foundation | 0.49 | 0.41–0.41 | New announced work; execution and cash terms ND |

The four dated letters imply ₹15.96–₹17.48 crore of incremental ex-GST work on the stated interpretation, not guaranteed unexecuted backlog at 20 October. Kanakia's revision is counted only for its ₹4.856 crore gross increment, not both old and revised totals. Kolte Patil's 'fresh work order' and extension wording does not settle whether the new ₹2.994 crore gross amount is additional to or replaces the ₹1.792 crore prior order. Both interpretations are retained. Contract margins, advances, retention percentages, completion dates, penalties and cancellation rights are ND.

Growth must earn a return after funding receivables, retention and machines. The public capital bridge produces incremental normalized NOPAT/IC of 22.1% over FY23–FY26 and 18.2% over FY24–FY26, versus an analyst 14–18% capital-cost range. That is positive evidence and supports a numerical CAP score. But FY26 alone fell to 6.3%, with an additional ₹8.90 crore of invested capital producing only ₹0.56 crore of incremental NOPAT. Much of the recent equipment may not yet be mature; neither its success nor its failure is proven.

The base forecast therefore slows growth to 10% in FY27 and 12% thereafter, keeps normalized EBITDA margin at 16% before added director costs, requires operating working capital of 22% of annual sales, maintenance capex at 3.5% of sales and growth capex of 12% of incremental sales. A bull case needs a better 18% margin and 19% working-capital ratio as well as faster execution. These are testable operating assumptions, not capacity already contracted and funded. GQS 6.4 reflects real growth with mixed cash and recent capital productivity.

sections.title: Management, governance and execution
sections.text:
Promoter ownership is 68.84%, or 9.059 million shares, after the FY25 rights issue. Family control can support continuity and commercial relationships; it also places a premium on related-party and remuneration disclosure. The April 2026 promoter declaration states no direct or indirect encumbrance was created during FY26. That is not a separately authenticated October pledge balance. The annual MGT-9 opening table appears to retain pre-rights holdings despite FY26 share-capital comparatives being unchanged: use the audited share-capital note and dated allotment evidence, not that opening column, to date dilution.

The March 2025 rights issue raised ₹6.9564 crore by issuing 6,324,000 shares at ₹11. It was 92.51% subscribed, below the initially proposed full 6,836,000-share offer. Share count increased 92.51%; a non-participating original owner's percentage interest fell about 48.05%. These are different measures. FY25 CARO says proceeds were used for their stated purposes. The original detailed rights use-of-proceeds document was not recovered, so no particular remaining investment is treated as unrestricted rights money. FY26 has no additional issued equity or optional warrant proceeds assumed.

FY25 disclosed director unsecured loans of ₹1.9664 crore and total unsecured borrowing of ₹2.0064 crore. FY26 unsecured borrowing is nil. Repayment of disclosed promoter funding is not automatically diversion. Interest, security and full transaction ledgers remain insufficiently granular. Actual FY26 director remuneration of ₹0.3069 crore is about 7.6% of PAT. September AGM approvals permit annual ceilings totaling ₹0.90 crore, not proof that this amount has been paid. The model adds ₹0.30 crore of recurring annual cost in the base from September, with zero and the full ₹0.5931 crore increment tested.

| Dated commitment / event | Observed delivery or counterevidence | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| FY25 broader heavy-civil ambition | FY26 services revenue and machine capex rose; new work remains largely Mumbai groundwork. | Delivery in the core niche; national diversification unproven. |
| March 2025 rights issue | Actual ₹6.9564cr received; cash initially built, then substantially deployed in FY26. | Financing delivered; returns on new deployment still mixed. |
| August 2024 auditor appointment | Prior two terms expired; successor clean main and IFC opinions. | Rotation, not an adverse resignation. |
| FY24 SH-7 filing exception | Later authorized capital is ₹15cr and FY26 secretarial audit does not repeat exception. | Later counterevidence, but filing receipt itself not inspected. |
| August 2026 price query | Issuer says all material information disclosed and movement is market-driven. | Response retained; no manipulation allegation inferred. |

No substantiated integrity failure or minority-abuse override is applied. The governance score stays mixed because recurring financial-note quality and limited RPT detail matter, even when the formal audit is clean.

sections.title: Financial forensics
sections.text:
| FY | Revenue | Core EBITDA | PAT | CFO reported | CFO adjusted* | Cash capex | Debt | Cash | Equity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 5.05 | -3.85 | -6.59 | 1.03 | -1.10 | 0.09 | 11.35 | 0.28 | 0.30 |
| 2022 | 5.39 | -1.92 | -4.13 | 1.12 | -1.42 | 0.01 | 11.96 | 0.06 | -3.83 |
| 2023 | 11.95 | 2.82 | 0.60 | 3.37 | 1.87 | 0.00 | 9.82 | 0.02 | -3.23 |
| 2024 | 14.31 | 3.29 | 1.16 | 0.36 | 1.20 | 0.60 | 9.38 | 0.10 | -2.07 |
| 2025 | 24.50 | 5.36 | 3.22 | 2.65 | 4.25 | 2.81 | 7.30 | 6.98 | 8.10 |
| 2026 | 41.56 | 6.72 | 4.03 | 1.18 | 0.45 | 4.99 | 5.70 | 0.13 | 12.13 |

All amounts are ₹crore. *Adjusted CFO removes short-term borrowing movements, deducts interest paid and reconstructs asset-sale classification where the reported signs conflict with the gain/loss notes. It is an analyst reconstruction, not an issuer restatement. Loss-year CFO/PAT ratios are not meaningful. No acquisition cash flows, leases or capital creditors are invented where they are not separately identified. Gross profit and separate contract assets are ND; recorded receivables and retention are included.

**Profit bridge.** FY25-to-FY26 PBT rose ₹1.516 crore: about ₹0.752 crore from operating EBIT before other income, ₹0.135 crore additional other income and ₹0.629 crore lower finance cost. The tax charge increased ₹0.709 crore, leaving PAT up ₹0.807 crore. Other income includes a ₹0.2451 crore creditor-balance writeback, which is excluded from core EBIT. Core EBITDA rose 25.3%, but its margin fell from 21.9% to 16.2%. Normalizing to 26% tax and removing non-operating income and disposal effects yields FY26 PAT of ₹3.249 crore, not ₹4.026 crore. DTA of ₹1.295 crore is not cash and does not establish a perpetual zero-tax rate.

Reported EPS declined from ₹4.66 to ₹3.06 because FY25 weighted-average shares were only 6.905 million versus 13.16 million in FY26. On the same current 13.16-million denominator, PAT per share increased from about ₹2.45 to ₹3.06. The rights issue cannot be counted as FY26 organic earnings growth or ignored when estimating investor economics.

**Cash classification.** FY24–FY26 reported CFO/PAT is 49.97%, which triggers investigation. Reclassifying short-term debt and interest raises it to 72.0%; asset-sale sign reconstruction gives 70.3%. Over FY23–FY26 the latter is 86.3%. The company did not report a fictitious negative operating cash result simply because it repaid debt through the CFO section. Conversely, FY26 after-interest operating cash of ₹0.454 crore is genuinely weak against ₹4.026 crore PAT. Receivables rose ₹4.861 crore and advances rose ₹0.878 crore while trade payables fell ₹0.617 crore. Capex explains cash depletion, not the collection shortfall.

**Cash bridge and obligations.** Opening ₹6.9831 crore + reported CFO ₹1.1844 crore − investing cash ₹5.7106 crore − financing cash ₹2.3228 crore = closing ₹0.1340 crore, within ₹1 rounding. Cash includes only ₹0.0216 crore in banks and ₹0.1124 crore on hand. Debt declined from ₹7.2973 crore to ₹5.7044 crore; current maturity is ₹1.1484 crore and overdraft ₹0.2369 crore. Net-debt/core-EBITDA is 0.83× and core EBIT/finance cost 5.88×. These solvency ratios are substantially better than the cash cushion.

Recorded statutory and tax claims total ₹1.6228 crore, against government balances of ₹1.3294 crore. The forecast settles the ₹0.29335 crore net once in FY27 and excludes both gross balances from operating NWC, avoiding double counting. This assumes timing/offset usability and is not proof of a legal netting right. Retention deposits of ₹1.5714 crore and unspecified noncurrent investments of ₹0.9740 crore are not free cash. No quantified contingent dispute, guarantee, separate gratuity liability or off-balance capital commitment was identified in the reviewed statements; a lack of granular disclosure is not positive evidence of zero exposure. Salary and retention payables remain in modeled NWC.

Closing receivable days increased to 95.8 from 90.1. Over-six-month receivables fell from ₹2.235 crore to ₹1.967 crore, now 18.0% of the total, with no doubtful allowance shown. This is better ageing in absolute terms alongside worse total cash absorption, not a simple all-bad narrative.

**Capital bridge.** Invested capital = equity + interest-bearing debt − cash − disclosed non-operating investment − DTA. It rose from ₹4.789 crore in FY23 to ₹5.276 crore FY24, ₹6.528 crore FY25 and ₹15.432 crore FY26. Retention, advances and financing through operating liabilities are retained. Normalized NOPAT is operating EBIT ×74%. The 3-year/2-year/1-year incremental returns are 22.1%/18.2%/6.3%, respectively. Negative equity in FY22–FY24 does not make the enterprise capital denominator negative after debt is included. A recent high ROCE based on small legacy capital is not used as proof of high incremental returns.

**Audit scope and reliability.** The entire FY26 main statutory report, IFC annexure, CARO annexure and audit-trail paragraph were inspected, along with FY25 counterparts and FY24 exceptions. Main and IFC opinions are unmodified. CARO reports no default, willful default, fraud, six-month statutory arrears or cash losses in FY25/FY26; term loans were used as intended. The bank-return comparison is inapplicable because working-capital limits did not exceed ₹5 crore, not a clean bank-return reconciliation. Audit-trail functionality was reported operational and no tampering observed. The one-year-liability statement is not a future funding guarantee.

FY24 has an additional ₹0.0638123 crore discrepancy between the PPE annual-charge column and P&L, and its net-block date headings appear reversed. The gross/accumulated balances and later comparatives reconcile the correct FY24 net balance. This is a dated disclosure error, not an additional claim of overstated assets. The FY25 PPE table's annual depreciation is ₹0.360306 crore versus P&L ₹0.828768 crore; FY26 is ₹0.918004 crore versus ₹1.427036 crore. The differences are 14.6% and 12.6% of the respective PAT. The aggregate P&L charge repeats in the separately filed results, and net PPE can be bridged with that charge and disposal NBV, so this is not evidence that earnings are overstated by those amounts. It remains a repeated material disclosure inconsistency requiring correction. Asset-disposal signs also distort CFO/CFI classification in FY23–FY25 while offsetting in total cash. FY25's wrong net-cash-change line is corrected in FY26 comparatives; FY24's director-summary PAT differs from its actual audited P&L and the later comparative, so we use the latter rather than call a new restatement. The G2 hold is about unresolved reliability, not a fraud finding.

sections.title: Valuation and market expectations
sections.text:
At the authenticated but stale ₹38.75, equity value is ₹50.995 crore. Enterprise value is ₹56.565 crore after adding ₹5.704 crore debt and deducting only ₹0.134 crore cash. The unidentified ₹0.974 crore investment receives no EV deduction or terminal realization credit. Reported P/E is 12.67×, normalized P/E 15.69×, EV/core-EBITDA 8.42× and P/B 4.20×. These are reference diagnostics, not a current executable quote or a margin of safety.

**Horizon and mechanism.** The model begins with the audited 31 March 2026 balance sheet and first bridges monthly to the 20 October entry. It then runs to exactly 20 October 2031, 1,826 holding days (4.9993 years using 365.25). FY32 is only a partial fiscal year in cash-flow rows; exit EBITDA is trailing 365-day modeled EBITDA, not the full FY32 run rate or an arbitrary fifth fiscal-year number. Equity exit value = multiple × TTM EBITDA + cash above the continuing ₹0.10 crore reserve − debt. It is divided by the actual whole-share count after all modeled issues. There are no dividends or unexplained terminal investment windfalls.

Bear/base/bull assumptions are respectively FY27 growth −10%/10%/25%, later growth 4%/12%/22%, operating EBITDA margin 12%/16%/18%, NWC 28%/22%/19% of revenue and terminal EV/EBITDA 4×/6×/8×. These margins precede incremental director costs of ₹0.5931/₹0.30/₹0.15 crore annually from September 2026. Common assumptions are 26% tax on positive PBT, 13% cost of existing debt, annual scheduled principal ₹1.1484 crore until repaid, depreciation 3.4% of revenue, maintenance capex 3.5% and growth capex 12% of incremental revenue. There is no unverified committed new debt or free promoter finance.

**Funding discipline.** Twenty-three percent of annual revenue is placed in April–September, close to FY26 experience; 77% falls in H2. Each interval prefunds capex, principal, positive working-capital investment and positive settlement of old statutory claims before operating realization. Interest, cash tax and any operating loss enter the end-cash test. Every interval must preserve the assumed reserve. Cash cannot fund expenditure that precedes receipt. Alternative sequencing, seasonality and cash reserves are tested rather than asserting daily cash is known.

All ordinary scenario returns and entry prices are null. Every non-rescue central case breaches the modeled reserve before entry, so its conditional non-rescue returns are also null, even if the eventual terminal value looks attractive. An explicit alternative issues whole shares at ₹27.125 (70% of the stale reference), with 2% financing fees, immediately before the particular interval's shortfall. This is hypothetical third-party equity, not a recommendation, committed financing, or an assertion that an actual April 2026 issue took place. Pre-entry and post-entry dilution are separated. Authorized-share headroom is checked, and no future proceeds are credited after the terminal date.

**Hypothetical funded alternatives only:**

| Case | Gross rescue ₹cr | Exit shares | Exit ₹/share | Conditional CAGR | 12% price | 15% price | 18% price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bear | 2.58 | 14111351 | 14.79 | -18.2% | 8.06 | 7.06 | 6.21 |
| Base | 1.19 | 13598973 | 58.42 | 7.7% | 31.85 | 27.91 | 24.54 |
| Bull | 1.30 | 13640541 | 140.08 | 28.3% | 76.38 | 66.92 | 58.84 |

The last three columns are scenario-dependent maximum entry-price diagnostics after 2% entry and 2% exit friction, not buy ranges. Base rescue costs ₹0.0238 crore in fees, supplies ₹1.1669 crore net and issues 438,973 shares, all before the modeled entry. Original-owner dilution is 3.23%; the hypothetical entrant already buys the resulting 13,598,973-share capitalization and has no additional base-case dilution after entry. The base's 7.7% annual return is below 15% despite assuming successful funding. Base 15%-hurdle diagnostic ₹27.91 is not a recommendation until the gates resolve.

**Base pre-entry bridge, all forecast, ₹crore:**

| Interval end | Revenue | Operating cash | Capex | Principal | Gross rescue | Closing cash |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-30 | 1.75 | 0.14 | 0.17 | 0.09 | 0.30 | 0.28 |
| 2026-05-31 | 1.75 | 0.14 | 0.18 | 0.10 | 0.16 | 0.28 |
| 2026-06-30 | 1.75 | 0.14 | 0.17 | 0.09 | 0.15 | 0.28 |
| 2026-07-31 | 1.75 | 0.14 | 0.18 | 0.10 | 0.16 | 0.28 |
| 2026-08-31 | 1.75 | 0.14 | 0.18 | 0.10 | 0.16 | 0.28 |
| 2026-09-30 | 1.75 | 0.13 | 0.17 | 0.09 | 0.15 | 0.26 |
| 2026-10-20 | 3.78 | 0.37 | 0.11 | 0.06 | 0.11 | 0.54 |

**Base funded annual flows, ₹crore:**

| FY | Revenue | EBITDA | Normalized PAT | Operating cash | Capex | Principal | Gross rescue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2027 | 45.71 | 7.14 | 3.64 | 4.27 | 2.10 | 1.15 | 1.19 |
| 2028 | 51.20 | 7.89 | 4.16 | 4.70 | 2.45 | 1.15 | 0.00 |
| 2029 | 57.34 | 8.87 | 4.85 | 5.45 | 2.74 | 1.15 | 0.00 |
| 2030 | 64.22 | 9.98 | 5.60 | 6.27 | 3.07 | 1.15 | 0.00 |
| 2031 | 71.93 | 11.21 | 6.43 | 7.18 | 3.44 | 1.11 | 0.00 |
| 2032 | 25.20 | 3.87 | 2.23 | 2.49 | 2.14 | 0.00 | 0.00 |

FY32 rows stop on 20 October 2031. Full monthly tables retain debt, PPE, NWC, taxes, fees, whole shares and identity residuals. Base forecast entry cash is ₹0.54 crore and debt ₹5.07 crore after the hypothetical rescue; neither is asserted to be an observed October balance.

**Reverse expectation.** With the base margin, NWC and capex rules, 6× exit multiple and explicit equity rescue, a finite 0%–60% annual-growth bracket crosses the ₹38.75 reference. The solution is **20.85% annual revenue growth**, requiring about **₹129.44 crore** of full FY32 annual revenue, **₹2.421 crore** gross rescue and **14,052,485** terminal shares. The reproduced price residual is -0.000000219951711623071362975261 rupees after 26 bisection steps. This is a funded expectation calculation, not a reverse case that borrows indefinitely at negative cash.

**Sensitivity.** Both funded and non-rescue branches rerun genuine 3×3 WC/maintenance-capex and growth/exit-multiple grids. Additional tests vary H1 sales share (23%/35%/50%), opening cash (₹0.134/1/2 crore), reserves (₹0/0.10/0.50 crore), extra collection delay (0/30/60 days), prefunding fraction (0%/50%/100%), equity issue-price fraction (50%/70%/90%), execution friction (0%/2%/5%) and incremental director remuneration. Gross statutory settlement is tested immediately versus uniformly, with government-credit realization at 0%/50%/100%; both assets and liabilities remain excluded from NWC. With immediate gross statutory payment and no government-credit recovery, base gross rescue rises to ₹2.680 crore and the conditional annual return falls to 6.9%. No later cash or terminal value is manufactured for an unrecovered credit. Changes recompute monthly funding, dilution, taxes, terminal equity and returns rather than only changing the terminal multiple.

sections.title: Bear case and permanent-loss path
sections.text:
The linked downside is not simply a lower exit multiple. A project certification delay or developer cash squeeze defers collection while machine expenses, subcontractors, statutory claims and debt instalments must still be paid. High fixed deployment costs and weaker contract terms reduce margin. Capex deferral can preserve cash temporarily but may constrain execution or equipment reliability. Director remuneration at the approved ceiling would compound the operating pressure. Additional equity, if available only at a deep discount, protects the company by diluting its owners.

The explicit bear combines a 10% revenue decline in FY27, 4% subsequent growth, 12% EBITDA margin, 28% working capital, the full incremental remuneration ceiling and 4× exit EV/EBITDA. It needs ₹2.58 crore gross equity support and ends at about ₹14.79 per share, a roughly −18.2% annual return after assumed friction. This is a funded survival scenario, not a guaranteed liquidation floor. Actual insolvency, asset impairment, contract penalties or inability to issue equity could be materially worse.

A 30-day extra receivable lockup ties up approximately one twelfth of first-year revenue before any additional margin loss. This stress and the government-credit recovery test show why a modest net-debt/EBITDA ratio does not establish cash safety. Physical machinery is not a cash-equivalent downside backstop: resale value, liens and the cost of idle equipment are unknown. No unverified forced-sale recovery is added.

Liquidity compounds rather than causes this fundamental risk. Only 27 of 60 authenticated session archives contain an issuer row; the other 33 cannot be labeled zero-trade sessions without additional confirmation. Only one of the last 20 sessions has an observed row. The last row was one 4,000-share trade. A nominal quoted value cannot guarantee an exit at that price, especially when an adverse event reduces bids. No market-manipulation or suspension conclusion is drawn.

sections.title: Five-times and ten-times feasibility
sections.text:
At ₹38.75, a 5× nominal share-price outcome is ₹193.75 and a 10× outcome ₹387.50. Over five years these require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annual share-price compounding before friction, respectively. They are not forecasts.

Even the explicit funded bull ends near ₹140.08 per share, around 3.6× the reference before execution friction. It already assumes 25% first-year growth, 22% thereafter, 18% operating margin, improved capital efficiency and 8× terminal EBITDA, above the base multiple. Five times therefore needs an even more favorable combination of scale, margin, collection and valuation; ten times would require a profound, presently unverified economic change. Issuing shares to fund the expansion makes revenue growth different from per-share wealth growth.

An accessible urban-redevelopment opportunity exists, and a small company can grow from a low base. But no project cohort, contracted machine utilization, protected pricing or funded national rollout establishes such a path. FY26 incremental NOPAT/IC of 6.3% cannot finance rapid compounding internally. MOAT 4, CAP 5 and BQS 5.3 are inconsistent with calling Manav a proven five-year 5×/10× compounder. The correct classification is a conditional execution-and-cash-recovery watchlist.

sections.title: Monitoring plan
sections.text:
| Item | Evidence that would improve the thesis | Evidence that would weaken it | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Financial reconciliation | Auditor/issuer schedules reconcile FY24–FY26 PPE annual charges, disposal NBV and cash-flow classification. | Another unexplained material note mismatch or adverse audit opinion. | Before any favorable reassessment. |
| Cash and obligations | Published September accounts and a reliable March-to-current bridge show collections, capex, gross statutory payments and available committed funding. | Maturity extension under distress, overdue statutory payments or further cash depletion. | Next available interim filing and debt disclosures. |
| Contract economics | Opening/intake/execution/closing backlog, ex-GST values, completion dates, advances and job margins; quantified top-customer share. | New headline orders without collection, or material cancellations/penalties. | Each material work order and results cycle. |
| Incremental returns | New machines and NWC produce sustained incremental NOPAT/IC above the 14–18% analytical capital-cost range. | Revenue growth with more capital absorption and falling normalized margin. | FY27 and subsequent audited periods. |
| Governance | Actual remuneration within disclosed approvals, full related-party loan terms, corrected ownership tables and investment detail. | Unexplained transfers, off-market related dealings or repeated uncorrected capital disclosures. | Each annual/interim related-party release. |
| Tradability | Current exact-ISIN quote, verified applicable restrictions and a complete recent session series support feasible whole-lot entry and exit. | Longer staleness, bid disappearance, lower lot-adjusted capacity or new restrictions. | Before any investment implementation. |

These are research triggers, not a claim that continuous monitoring has been scheduled. No alert threshold converts an assumed reserve into a contractual covenant. A current price alone is insufficient: both the underlying gate and the supporting evidence must change.

sections.title: Final classification and conditional action
sections.text:
**Classification: Hold — unresolved; conditional execution-and-cash-recovery watchlist.** Do not rank the company as investable or as a proven compounder. The clean audit conclusions, organic execution rebound and repeat orders deserve credit, but do not offset financial-note reconciliation, present funding and tradability gaps. Conversely, those gaps do not justify inventing fraud, a default, persistent negative incremental returns or a punitive numerical score cap.

For a new purchase, ordinary expected return and entry price remain NS/null. The ₹27.91 base 15%-hurdle diagnostic applies only to the specific hypothetical equity-funded model. It is neither a target price nor a gate override. A verified September cash bridge, consistent accounting, committed financing where needed and feasible lot-adjusted execution could restore ordinary scenario analysis. The model should then be rerun with the actual capitalization and a current verified price, not merely reuse a stale discount percentage.

For an existing investor, this research does not know position size, cost basis, risk capacity or tax situation and does not prescribe an order. A ₹500,000 research position rounds down to three lots/12,000 shares/₹465,000 or up to four lots/16,000 shares/₹620,000 at the reference. Observed mean turnover is ₹236,874 and observed median ₹179,400, but those are only for the 27 matched sessions. The often tempting 55.7-session 5%-participation estimate is only an observed-row continuous-share illustration, not a full-window exit estimate. No observed session, including the 20,000-share maximum, permits even one 4,000-share lot at 2%, 5% or 10% participation. The missing 33 rows are not zero-filled. L stays NS and G4 remains unresolved.

sections.title: Sources, assumptions and open questions
sections.text:
The source ledger below links primary issuer/exchange/credit-rating records and three primary peer reports. Evidence IDs map each scored claim to document locators. Original downloads were inspected locally, with hashes retained. Financial and market facts are limited to what was available by 20 October 2026; downloads on 22 October are retrieval dates, not permission to use later events. The official security-master URL is dated 19 October and was retrieved on 22 October; the lot is independently verified in the 5 October bhavcopy, without relying on a live cutoff surveillance assertion. The FY25 J. Kumar comparison is explicitly older than the FY26 peer reports.

Reported facts, calculations and forecasts are separate: annual balances and dated order terms are reported; core earnings, CFO reclassification and incremental returns are analyst calculations; margins, tax normalization, financing, issue discount, timing, reserves and exit multiples are assumptions. The calculations can be independently reproduced from the disclosed inputs; reproduction does not independently verify the forecast assumptions.

Open questions with investment consequences: (1) reconcile PPE year charges and CFS asset-sale signs; (2) identify the ₹0.974 crore investment and any restrictions; (3) reconcile actual September cash, collections, capex, gross statutory dues and available bank lines; (4) disclose customer concentration, project margins, retention release and backlog rollforward; (5) verify actual remuneration and detailed related-party terms; (6) establish a current exact-security quote, restrictions and complete session-level trading observations. These are missing facts, not asserted adverse outcomes. No fallback analyst forecast, unspecified peer multiple, assumed fundraise or invented zero volume fills the gap.

The complete reproducible model retains both funded and unfunded paths, financial history, score arithmetic, evidence map and sensitivity outputs. This is research, not individualized investment advice or an execution instruction.

funding_rules.reserve: 0.10 crore analyst reserve, varied0/0.50; not regulatory minimum
funding_rules.cash_order: Monthly capex, principal, positive old statutory settlement and positive working-capital uses are prefunded at start. Operating realization, including interest, tax and any operating loss, is tested at interval end. Government recovery is not an upfront financing source. Sensitivity allows partial/end-interval sequencing. Ordinary negative path is a diagnostic, not an assumed overdraft.
funding_rules.equity: If rescue selected, whole shares issued at70%of₹38.75 with2%fees before interval uses. No actual lender or shareholder commitment is assumed. Gross/fees/net and pre/post-entry dilution separate.
funding_rules.tax: 26%ofpositivePBT; no DTA cash credited. March government asset ₹1.3294 crore and statutory/tax claims ₹1.6228 crore are excluded from operating NWC. Base assumes both settle proportionately through FY27, not legal fungibility. Sensitivities test 0%, 50% and 100% recovery against uniform or immediate gross payment; no later recovery or terminal credit for unrecovered balances.
funding_rules.investments: ₹0.974cr unspecified noncurrent investments get zero free-cash or terminal credit.
funding_rules.cash_deficit: Any cash floor breach, including prior to entry, makes non-rescue conditional returns and prices null. Ordinary investment returns are null irrespective of scenario because gates unresolved.
